title.narrative: Provision integrated Emergency Health and Nutrition Response to Mitigate Drought Impacts in Xudur and Buur Hakaba Districts, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed intervention will provide emergency, life-saving health and nutrition services to drought-affected populations in Xudur and Buurhakaba—priority districts in southern Somalia experiencing severe humanitarian need.ltbrgtThe project will reduce excess morbidity and mortality by expanding integrated health and nutrition services through static facilities, mobile outreach teams, community case management, and strengthened referral systems. Nutrition activities will be implemented in Burhakaba focusing on mass screening, early detection, and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and women of reproductive age in Burhakaba. Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) will be treated through outpatient therapeutic programmes (OTP), iCCM+, and stabilisation care for complications. Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) will be managed through targeted supplementary feeding (TSFP), improved home diets using the Kobciye Shurbad model, micronutrient supplementation (MNPs, MMS), and IYCF counselling through Care Groups to improve feeding and caregiving practices.ltbrgtThe health component will operate in both districts to improve access to essential primary and referral-level services for rural and hard-to-reach populations. Core activities include outpatient consultations, essential medicines, mental health and psychosocial support, antenatal care, skilled deliveries, emergency obstetric care including caesarean sections, and strengthened routine immunisation supported by functioning cold chain systems. The project will reinforce referral pathways for complex medical and nutritional cases. Community outreach and supervision will enable sustained service delivery in villages with poor access to health facilities.ltbrgtThe intervention will target vulnerable host, IDP, and rural communities. Outreach teams will regularly visit 3 rural villages in Hudur (Wanay village, Shiilow village and Gaabiney village) and 3 in Burhakaba (Sool Village, Awyaaaye. Village and Bisley. Village), while static facilities will serve urban and peri-urban poor. Due to insecurity, 10 long-distance rural villages will be supported through iCCM outreach: 5 inltbrgtShidle Gomorey GabaneyCusbo eelo Waney ) and 5 in Burhakaba (Aw-ooyowKurow Aw Riikow Ibooti Awyaaye donki Arey wiin).ltbrgtThe project aims to reach 97,467 people across both districts, prioritising children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women, women of reproductive age, and vulnerable households. Key targets include screening 21,845 individuals for malnutrition, treating 3,050 SAM cases, and supporting 8,738 MAM cases with specialised and home-based dietary support. Health services will deliver approximately 44,940 outpatient consultations, 8,799 antenatal care visits, 636 skilled deliveries, 1,500 child immunisations, and 20,000 treatment courses. Outreach teams will conduct at least 317 service delivery days to expand coverage in underserved settlements.ltbrgtBy restoring access to critical services, addressing treatment gaps, and strengthening facility and community systems, the intervention will reduce preventable disease and malnutrition-related deaths, improve health outcomes, and support resilience among affected households.The project aligns with health and nutrition cluster priorities and OCHA reserve allocation objectives, ensuring an integrated, conflict-sensitive response tailored to urgent needs in the most severely affected locations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
